title: Runtime sequence-length guide & pad-eviction scheduler
creator: Ari Turner
description: Design and implement a runtime component that groups incoming requests into dynamic sequence-length cohorts ("seqlen-guides") and evicts/reclaims padding via a pad-eviction scheduler. The goal is to reduce wasted tokens (padding) across prefill+decode flows while exposing lightweight kernel-selection hints to the serving runtime. This work ties kernel hinting, attention optimization choices (fused vs block-sparse), and prefill/decode scheduling so that we can aggressively shrink micro-batch shapes without regressing latency SLOs or increasing tail variance.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration exists in runtime staging and can be toggled per-model via config
Token-padding overhead reduced by >= 12% on 5 representative production workloads compared to baseline
Median p99.9 latency impact <= +5% for decode paths on small/medium traffic profiles
Kernel selection annotations are surfaced in trace spans and appear in Console per-request breakdowns
Automated canary rollout and rollback implemented (feature flag + rollout policy)
design_decisions: Cohort grouping will use a two-stage policy: fast histogram bucketing (O(1)) at admission, then occasional reclustering based on runtime seqlen drift
Prefill-aware packer: prefill sequences get higher eviction priority to maximize KV cache reuse; decoder-only streaming requests are grouped into lean cohorts
Kernel hints: runtime exposes 'kernel_hint' header values ("fused_attention" | "block_sparse" | "fp16_fastpath")
Pad-eviction uses token budget windows: if a cohort's pad ratio exceeds threshold X for >Y seconds, evict and re-batch smaller cohorts
Fallback safety: on high tail latency or CUDA OOM signals, auto-disable aggressive eviction and revert to conservative bucketing
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Ticket created after spike session with Research and Runtime teams; baseline padding audit added to ticket
2025-11-11: Prototype histogram bucketer implemented (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3123); initial offline tests show 9% pad reduction on conversational dataset
2025-11-18: Kernel hint API sketched; security review requested for header propagation (sec flagged leakage risk)
2025-11-25: Benchmarked fused_attention vs block_sparse across sequence ranges; fused wins on short sequences (<128) while block_sparse favorably trades memory for long sequences (>1024)
2025-12-02: Integration tests added for canary rollout; telemetry events emitted to staging Console dashboard (links below)
todos: Finish pad-eviction scheduler to respect per-customer reserved capacity limits
Add metrics for pad-eviction churn (evictions/sec) and cohort-stability (median lifetime)
Wire kernel_hint to serving decision engine and update kernel-selector mapping table
Create PRD blurb for product to communicate expected cost savings to customers
Run canary for 48h on low-risk tier and collect p50/p95/p99 latency + token-savings
rollout_plan: Stage -> Canary (5% low-tier traffic) for 48h -> Gradual ramp to 25% -> Full roll (with opt-out flag). Automatic rollback triggers on p99 latency regression >10% or CUDA OOM rate >0.1%
performance_targets: Reduce padded tokens by >=12% across workload mix, improve per-token cost by >=6%, maintain median latency within +3% and p99 within +5%
risks: Aggressive pad eviction may increase tail variance during bursts
Incorrect kernel_hint mapping could choose slower kernels for given seqlen leading to regressions
Security: header-based hints could leak internal routing if mishandled
Edge-case: streaming decode requests with very long prefixes may fragment cohorts and reduce batching efficiency
